blocks.text: The psalm begins by calling the speaker’s own soul to bless the LORD and to remember his benefits. The opening catalogues forgiveness, healing, rescue, steadfast love, mercy, and renewed strength, framing praise as a response to what the LORD has done.

The scope then widens beyond personal benefit. The LORD’s righteous acts and justice for the oppressed are linked with what was made known to Moses and Israel. Later, human life is pictured as dust, grass, and a fading flower, while the LORD’s steadfast love and covenant faithfulness endure. The final summons expands still further: angels, heavenly hosts, servants, and all works in the LORD’s dominion are called to bless him.

Verses 8–13 describe the LORD as compassionate, gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in steadfast love. This language has been understood as drawing on a familiar confession about the LORD’s character. The father-and-children comparison and the distance between east and west portray compassion in terms of the removal of transgressions rather than unending judgment.
